description: The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 15 to 22 June is below 1% over most of the west, northwest and centre, against 90 to 100% along the eastern border and the coast. From 22 June to 27 July the north-centre stays at 1 to 10% and the west at 10 to 45%, while the east holds 55 to 90% with cells of 90 to 99% on the Somali border near the equator between 29 June and 13 July. The south rises to 55 to 90% from 29 June.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 28 June to 5 July is below 10% over most of the north, centre and west, with 75 to 99% only over the central highlands on the equator and in the southwest near 3S. For 5 to 12 July probabilities rise to 75 to 99% along the coast and the eastern border from 4.5S to 2N, while the north-centre stays below 10%. From 12 July to 9 August the north-centre and the area along 37.5E north of the equator stay at 1 to 25%, while the south and east hold 55 to 90%, with 75 to 90% on the coast near 3S and over the central highlands on the equator.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 5 to 12 July is above 99% across the south, the central highlands on the equator and the northeast between 1N and 4N, against below 1% in the north-centre and northwest. From 12 July to 2 August the north-centre stays below 10% and the west and centre at 10 to 45%, while the south and east hold 55 to 90%, with 90 to 99% on the coast near 3S in the week of 19 to 26 July. For 2 to 16 August most of Kenya is at 45 to 75%, with 90 to 99% over the central highlands on the equator in the last week and 1 to 25% near Lake Victoria and in the north-centre.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 28 July to 4 August is below 1% across most of the north, centre and east, against 90 to 99% in the central highlands on the equator and near Lake Victoria at 1.5S. From 4 to 25 August the north and west stay at 0 to 25%, while the east along the Somali border rises to 55 to 90% and the coast near 3S reaches 90 to 99%. From 25 August to 8 September the west and north remain at 1 to 45%, with 55 to 90% in the east and on the coast and 90 to 99% in the far southwest near 4.5S.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 15 to 22 August is below 10% across the northwest and north-centre but 90 to 100% in the east and northeast and near the southern border around 37.5E. The west and northwest stay at 1 to 25% through 12 September, while the east holds 55 to 90%, highest along the Somali border and the coast. From 12 to 26 September the northwest recovers slightly to 10 to 45% and the coast near 3S reaches 90 to 99%.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 28 August to 4 September is below 1% over the west, northwest and centre, against above 99% along the eastern border, the coast and the southeast. From 4 to 25 September the west stays at 1 to 45%, while probabilities in the east and on the coast near 3S rise to 75 to 99%. From 25 September to 9 October the east holds 75 to 90% and the central highlands on the equator 90 to 99%, while the northwest stays at 10 to 45%.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 5 to 12 September is below 1% over much of the west and centre and 1 to 10% in the northwest, with 75 to 99% only along the eastern border. From 12 September to 3 October the west and northwest remain at 1 to 45%, while the east and coast hold 75 to 99%, peaking above 99% on the south coast near 3S. From 3 to 17 October probabilities rise to 55 to 90% over most of the country, with 90 to 99% in the central highlands on the equator and near 3N in the north, and 25 to 45% only in the far north and northwest.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 20 to 27 September is above 99% over the east, centre and coast, against 1 to 25% in the west and northwest, falling below 1% near 3N 36E. For 27 September to 4 October the west stays at 10 to 45% while the east holds 90 to 99%, peaking above 99% on the equator near 37.5E. From 4 October to 1 November probabilities are 75 to 99% over most of the country, with cells above 99% over the central highlands on the equator, and only small patches of 45 to 75% in the north and the far southwest.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 1 to 8 October is above 99% across the centre, east, coast and south, against only 1 to 25% in the northwest near Lake Turkana and in the far west. For 8 to 15 October probabilities are 75 to 99% over most of the east, coast and central highlands, peaking above 99% near 37.5E on the equator, while the far north stays at 10 to 45%. From 15 October to 12 November nearly the whole country sits at 55 to 90%, with 90 to 99% cells in the central highlands on the equator and in the southwest, and 25 to 55% only in isolated cells in the west.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 5 to 12 October is above 99% across the centre, east, coast and south, against only 10 to 45% in the northwest near Lake Turkana. For 12 to 19 October 75 to 99% persists in the east, along the coast and in the west near 1.5N, with 25 to 45% in the north-centre and the far southwest. Probabilities fall to 25 to 55% over much of the centre and north for 19 to 26 October, before returning to 55 to 90% nearly everywhere from 26 October to 16 November, with 90 to 99% cells in the central highlands and near the southern border.

The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 11 to 18 October is 90 to 100% over the eastern half and northeast, the west near 1.5N and the central highlands on the equator, but only 1 to 25% in the far southwest across the Tanzanian border. For 18 to 25 October the north drops to 10 to 45% north of 3N, while probabilities south of 1.5N are 75 to 99% and peak above 99% in central Kenya on the equator. From 25 October to 22 November most of the country sits at 55 to 90%, with 90 to 99% along and south of the southern border up to 8 November.

The ensemble mean for 15 to 29 January is 10 to 20 mm below the model-climate median in the southwest along the Tanzanian border, with deficits of 25 to 38 mm further south in northern Tanzania, and close to the median in the north. The deficits fade in the week of 29 January to 5 February. From 5 to 26 February the anomaly turns positive, at +10 to +20 mm over southwest Kenya, +8 to +12 mm in the central highlands and +25 to +38 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain.

The ensemble mean for 10 to 17 February is close to the model-climate median over nearly all of Kenya, with a surplus of 30 to 40 mm only at the western edge over Lake Victoria near 1.5S. For 17 February to 3 March positive anomalies spread over the southwest, the central highlands and northern Tanzania, reaching +60 to +70 mm at the western edge near 1.5S and +30 to +45 mm over the central highlands and south of the border. From 3 to 24 March anomalies weaken to +5 to +25 mm across the southwest and centre, with the north and east near zero throughout.

The ensemble mean for 5 to 12 March is above the model-climate median almost everywhere, by +40 to +65 mm across the south and southwest and up to +80 mm near the southern border around 3S 37.5E, and by +20 to +40 mm over the west and north. From 12 March to 2 April anomalies weaken to +5 to +20 mm over most of Kenya, with +25 to +35 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria. For 2 to 16 April anomalies are near zero to +15 mm, with slight deficits near Lake Victoria and in the far southwest.

The ensemble mean for 20 to 27 March is above the model-climate median everywhere, by 20 to 45 mm over most of Kenya, 50 to 60 mm in the west near the Uganda border and on the south coast, and up to about 85 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain. For 27 March to 3 April the surplus falls to 5 to 20 mm and the southwest across the Tanzanian border turns slightly negative (-5 to -10 mm). Weak positive anomalies of 5 to 20 mm persist from 3 April to 1 May, with a small deficit on the Lake Victoria shore at the equator.

The ensemble mean for 10 to 24 April is below the model-climate median over most of the west and north, by 15 to 20 mm in the first week and 25 to 35 mm near Lake Victoria between the equator and 2S in the week of 17 to 24 April, with a surplus only offshore near 5S. For 24 April to 8 May anomalies turn positive over most of Kenya, at +10 to +20 mm across the north and +20 to +30 mm at the western edge near Lake Victoria and over the central highlands on the equator, while 34.5E on the equator stays about 15 mm below. From 8 to 22 May anomalies are small, with +15 to +25 mm at the western edge near 1.5S and near-zero values elsewhere.

The ensemble mean for 20 to 27 April is 15 to 30 mm below the model-climate median in the west and southwest between the equator and 2S, and 30 to 40 mm above it on the south coast. For 27 April to 4 May the anomaly turns positive over most of the west and centre (+20 to +35 mm), reaching +40 to +55 mm over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain. From 4 May to 1 June anomalies stay within about 10 mm of the median, apart from a persistent deficit of 15 to 25 mm in the cell on the Lake Victoria shore at the equator.

The ensemble mean for 5 to 12 May is about 25 mm above the model-climate median over the central highlands on the equator and 10 to 15 mm above it near Lake Victoria, but 15 to 20 mm below it at 34.5E on the equator and 25 to 40 mm below it along the coast and offshore south of 2S. For 12 to 19 May the west near the Uganda border between 1N and 3N and the central highlands are 15 to 20 mm above the median, while the coast is 5 to 10 mm below. From 19 May to 16 June anomalies are small, with deficits of 10 to 15 mm at 34.5E on the equator and in the northwest and a slight surplus of 5 to 10 mm on the coast near 3S.

The ensemble mean for 25 May to 1 June is about 40 mm above the model-climate median on the coast near 3S and 25 to 35 mm above it along the rest of the coast, while the west near Lake Victoria and the northwest are 10 to 15 mm below. For 1 to 8 June the western edge over Lake Victoria and the area near 2N on the Uganda border are 15 to 20 mm above the median, with +15 to +20 mm on the coast near 3S. From 8 June to 6 July the coast near 3S stays 10 to 15 mm above the median and the west near 34.5E on the equator 5 to 15 mm below it, with near-zero anomalies elsewhere.

The ensemble mean for 15 to 22 June is 25 to 31 mm above the model-climate median on the north coast and the adjacent Somali border and 10 to 15 mm above it along the eastern border up to 3N, against deficits of 15 to 25 mm in the west and northwest along the Uganda border. From 22 June to 27 July the western deficits ease to 5 to 15 mm, largest near Lake Victoria on the equator, and the coastal surplus settles at 8 to 15 mm near 3S. The centre and south stay close to the median.

The ensemble mean for 28 June to 5 July is 10 to 15 mm below the model-climate median in the west near Lake Victoria at the equator and along the northwest border, with near-zero anomalies elsewhere. For 5 to 12 July the coast near 3S is about 15 mm above the median and the western edge over Lake Victoria 10 to 15 mm above it, while the northwest is 10 to 18 mm below. From 12 July to 9 August deficits of 10 to 15 mm persist in the northwest and near 34.5E on the equator, while the central highlands on the equator and the coast near 3S are 5 to 10 mm above the median.

The ensemble mean for 5 to 12 July is 10 to 20 mm below the model-climate median in the northwest and over the Ethiopian border, and 10 to 15 mm above it on the south coast near 3S to 5S. From 12 July to 2 August the deficits of 10 to 15 mm extend down the west to the equator, while the western edge over Lake Victoria and the coast near 3S are 10 to 20 mm above the median. For 2 to 16 August the central highlands on the equator turn +10 to +15 mm above the median, the west near 34.5E on the equator stays 10 to 15 mm below it, and the rest of Kenya is within 5 mm of zero.

The ensemble mean for 28 July to 4 August is 10 to 15 mm below the model-climate median in the northwest and the north, but 10 to 15 mm above it near Lake Victoria at 1.5S and in the central highlands on the equator. From 4 August to 8 September the strongest deficits, about -20 mm, sit in the west just north of the equator near 34.5E and along the northern border, while the coast near 3S is 5 to 10 mm above the median. Anomalies elsewhere in the centre and east stay within 5 mm of zero.

The ensemble mean for 15 to 22 August is 10 to 15 mm below the model-climate median in the west and northwest and 5 to 12 mm above it on the coast and in the northeast. The deficit deepens to 15 to 23 mm in the west near Lake Victoria on the equator from 22 August to 12 September, with a small surplus of 5 to 12 mm on the coast near 3S. From 12 to 26 September the deficit is limited to the cell west of 35E on the equator, while surpluses of 10 to 18 mm develop on the north coast and 5 to 10 mm over the east.

The ensemble mean for 28 August to 11 September is 20 to 35 mm below the model-climate median in the west and northwest, largest near Lake Victoria and the Uganda border, while the coast near 3S is about 15 mm above it. The western deficits ease to 10 to 20 mm by 25 September, and the coast stays at +10 to +15 mm. By 2 to 9 October anomalies turn positive over most of Kenya, at +15 to +20 mm in the northeast, the west near 1.5N, the central highlands and the coast near 3S.

The ensemble mean for 5 to 12 September is 15 to 30 mm below the model-climate median over the west and northwest, with near-zero anomalies in the east. From 12 September to 3 October deficits of 10 to 20 mm persist in the west near Lake Victoria and the far north, while the coast is 10 to 20 mm above the median. From 3 to 17 October anomalies turn positive nearly everywhere, reaching about +40 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N, +30 mm on the coast near 3S and +25 to +30 mm over the central highlands on the equator in the week of 10 to 17 October.

The ensemble mean for 20 September to 4 October is near or slightly below the model-climate median over the west and northwest (0 to -15 mm), while the coast near 3S is about +50 mm above it. For 4 to 18 October positive anomalies spread nationwide, with about +50 mm on the coast near 3S, +40 to +45 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N and +30 to +40 mm over the central highlands on the equator. From 18 October to 1 November the largest anomalies of +40 to +50 mm sit over the central highlands and the west, with +20 to +35 mm across the rest of Kenya.

The ensemble mean for 1 to 8 October is +30 to +40 mm above the model-climate median on the coast near 3S and +20 to +30 mm over the northeast, but 5 to 20 mm below it in the northwest. The wettest anomalies come for 8 to 22 October, about +60 mm on the south coast near 3S and +40 to +50 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N and over the central highlands on the equator. From 22 October to 12 November anomalies of +20 to +45 mm persist over the central highlands and the southwest, while the north and east stay at 0 to +20 mm.

The ensemble mean for 5 to 12 October is above the model-climate median almost everywhere, by +40 to +50 mm on the south coast near 3S and +30 to +40 mm over the northeast and central highlands, with small deficits of about -10 mm only in the far northwest. The largest anomalies come for 12 to 19 October, at about +60 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N and on the south coast near 3S. From 19 October to 16 November anomalies are smaller, mostly 0 to +20 mm, reaching +25 to +40 mm over the central highlands and the southwest, with slight deficits near Lake Victoria in the weeks to 2 November.

The ensemble mean for 11 to 18 October is about 80 mm above the model-climate median in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N and 30 to 60 mm above it along the eastern border and the coast, with near-zero anomalies in the centre and slightly negative values in the far southwest. For 18 to 25 October the largest positive anomaly (+30 to +50 mm) is over central Kenya on the equator, while the area north of 3N is slightly drier than the median (-5 to -15 mm). From 25 October to 22 November anomalies of +10 to +40 mm persist over the south and southwest, largest across the Tanzanian border, and the north stays near zero.

The tercile balance for 15 to 22 June shows a very strong split, with a below-normal lean of -75 to -100 points across the whole west, northwest and centre and an above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points from the Somali border to the coast. From 22 June to 27 July the below-normal lean of -50 to -100 points persists over the north-centre and northwest, while the east and the coast stay at +40 to +75 points. The southwest turns neutral to slightly above normal (+25 to +50 points) from 29 June onward.

The tercile balance for 28 June to 5 July leans strongly below normal (-75 to -100 points) over the north-centre and northwest between 2N and 5N, with only small above-normal cells of +50 to +75 points over the central highlands on the equator and in the east near 0.5N. For 5 to 26 July the north-centre stays strongly below normal at -75 to -100 points, while the coast near 3S and the east near the Somali border lean above normal at +75 to +100 points. From 26 July to 9 August the below-normal lean narrows to a band along 37.5E north of 2N and the west near Lake Victoria (-60 to -80 points), with +60 to +80 points over the central highlands on the equator and the coast near 3S.

The tercile balance for 5 to 12 July leans strongly above normal (+75 to +100 points) over the south, the central highlands and the east between the equator and 4N, against a strong below-normal lean of -75 to -100 points over the northwest and north-centre. From 12 July to 2 August the below-normal lean dominates the north-centre and west of 38E (-60 to -100 points), while the southwest near Lake Victoria and the coast near 3S lean above normal at +50 to +90 points. For 2 to 16 August the signal is weaker and mixed, with -50 to -75 points in the north-centre and near Lake Victoria and +50 to +80 points over the central highlands on the equator, the coast near 3S and the southwest.

The tercile balance for 28 July to 4 August leans very strongly below normal (-75 to -100 points) over most of Kenya, with an above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points only in the central highlands on the equator near 37.5E and the far southwest near Lake Victoria. From 4 to 25 August the north and northwest keep a strong below-normal lean (-60 to -100 points), while the east and the coast near 3S turn above normal at +40 to +90 points. From 25 August to 8 September the below-normal lean continues over the west and north (-50 to -80 points), and the coast near 3S, the central highlands and the southwest near 4.5S lean above normal at +50 to +90 points.

A sharp west to east contrast marks 15 to 22 August, with a below-normal lean of -75 to -100 points over the northwest and north-centre and an above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points in the east and northeast along the Somali border and the coast. The below-normal lean of -60 to -100 points persists over the west and northwest through 12 September, while the east and coast stay at +40 to +75 points. From 12 to 26 September the western signal weakens to -30 to -70 points and the eastern above-normal lean holds.

The tercile balance for 28 August to 4 September leans very strongly below normal (-90 to -100 points) across the west, northwest and centre, against a strong above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points over the east and the coast. The west and northwest keep a below-normal lean of -50 to -90 points through 25 September, while the above-normal lean in the east weakens to +25 to +75 points. From 25 September to 9 October the dipole fades, with a moderate above-normal lean of +40 to +75 points along the east and the coast, near +90 points over the central highlands on the equator, and only a weak below-normal lean left in the west and north.

The tercile balance for 5 to 12 September leans strongly below normal (-75 to -100 points) over the west, northwest and centre, against an above-normal lean of +50 to +90 points along the eastern border and the coast. From 12 September to 3 October the west and northwest keep a below-normal lean of -50 to -90 points, while the east and the coast stay above normal at +50 to +100 points. From 3 to 17 October the lean turns weakly to moderately above normal across most of the country (+25 to +75 points), strongest over the central highlands on the equator, with only near-neutral values in the northwest.

The tercile balance for 20 to 27 September is split, with a strong above-normal lean of +75 to +100 points over the east, centre and coast and a below-normal lean of -50 to -90 points across the west and northwest. For 27 September to 4 October the west and northwest still lean below normal (-25 to -75 points), while the east and the central highlands stay at +50 to +100 points. From 4 October to 1 November the lean turns above normal almost everywhere, at +40 to +100 points, strongest over the central highlands on the equator, the west near 1.5N and the east, with only near-zero values left in the far northwest.

The tercile balance for 1 to 8 October leans very strongly above normal (+90 to +100 points) across the centre, east, coast and south, while the northwest and the area near Lake Turkana lean below normal at -50 to -90 points. For 8 to 15 October the above-normal lean holds at +60 to +100 points in the east, northeast and central highlands, with a weaker below-normal lean of -25 to -60 points left in the far north. From 15 October to 12 November the lean is moderately above normal almost everywhere (+25 to +75 points), strongest in the west near 1.5N, over the central highlands on the equator and in the southwest, with only small near-zero patches.

The tercile balance for 5 to 12 October leans very strongly toward above normal (+75 to +100 points) across the centre, east, coast and south, with a below-normal lean of -25 to -75 points only in the far northwest near Lake Turkana. For 12 to 19 October the above-normal lean persists at +50 to +100 points in the east and northeast, the west near 1.5N and the central highlands, with a weak below-normal lean in the north-centre and the far southwest. From 19 October onward the signal weakens, with a slight below-normal lean (-10 to -40 points) through the centre and north in the week of 19 to 26 October and a moderate above-normal lean of +25 to +60 points, strongest in the south and southwest, in the weeks to 16 November.

The tercile balance for 11 to 18 October leans strongly above normal (+75 to +100 points) over the east, northeast and coast, the west near the Uganda border and the central highlands on the equator, against a below-normal lean of -50 to -90 points in the far southwest across the Tanzanian border. For 18 to 25 October the north flips to below normal (-30 to -75 points north of 3N), while the area south of 1.5N stays above normal at +50 to +100 points, peaking in central Kenya near the equator. From 25 October to 22 November a moderate above-normal lean of +25 to +75 points persists over the south and southwest, with little signal in the north.

Observed CHIRPS anomalies were mixed from 8 to 14 September, then turned 25 to 100 mm wetter than normal in the far west of the domain and over the northern Ethiopian highlands in the week of 15 to 21 September. By 29 September to 5 October the northern and western Ethiopian highlands were 25 to 100 mm drier than normal, consistent with rains ending early there, while southern Somalia was 100 to 200 mm wetter than normal. Around Lake Victoria and in western Kenya deficits of 10 to 50 mm persisted through the period.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall from 8 September to 5 October was heaviest over the Ethiopian highlands, South Sudan, Uganda and the western part of the domain, at 40 to 100 mm per week with local totals above 100 mm, while eastern Kenya, most of Somalia and Tanzania stayed largely dry. The Ethiopian maximum weakened and contracted southward week by week. The week of 29 September to 5 October stood out for a concentrated maximum of 150 to 200 mm in southern Somalia and for rain of 20 to 50 mm spreading south into western Tanzania.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall was 10 to 50 mm below normal around the Lake Victoria basin in each of the four weeks from 8 September to 5 October, with the largest deficits on the lake shore from 15 September onward. The east near the Somali border was 50 to 100 mm wetter than normal in the week of 15 to 21 September and 10 to 50 mm wetter in the following week. In the week of 29 September to 5 October the western highlands north of the equator recorded a surplus of 25 to 100 mm, while the south coast was 10 to 25 mm below normal.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall from 8 September to 5 October was concentrated in the west around the Lake Victoria basin and the western highlands at 20 to 50 mm per week, with a secondary area of 15 to 40 mm on the coast during the first three weeks. The week of 15 to 21 September also brought a local maximum above 75 mm in the east near the Somali border around the equator. In the week of 29 September to 5 October the western maximum shifted north of the lake to the highlands near 1N, where 75 to 150 mm fell, while the coast dried out and light totals of 5 to 15 mm reached the northeast.

There is no EFI shading anywhere in this forecast, so no wet-extreme signal is indicated. SOT contours appear only along the Uganda border near 1.5N and at the western edge near 1.5S for 24 April to 1 May, and around the central highlands on the equator near 37.5E for 1 to 8 May, without supporting EFI. The panels for 10 to 24 April and 8 to 22 May show nothing of note.

No wet-extreme signal is present for 20 to 27 April. For 27 April to 4 May the EFI reaches 0.6 to 0.7 over Lake Victoria at the western edge of the domain between 0.5N and 2S, with a SOT zero contour, and about 0.6 in one cell in central Kenya on the equator. No EFI shading above 0.5 appears from 4 May to 1 June, apart from a very small SOT contour in central Kenya for 4 to 11 May.

There is almost no wet-extreme signal in this forecast. The only shading is a single cell of EFI about 0.65 over the central highlands on the equator near 37.5E for 5 to 12 May, which weakens to about 0.55 with an SOT 0 contour for 12 to 19 May, and all panels from 19 May to 16 June are blank.

Only a weak wet-extreme signal is present. For 25 May to 1 June the EFI reaches 0.55 to 0.6 on the coast between 1S and 4S, with a fainter signal over the central highlands on the equator. For 1 to 8 June small cells of EFI 0.55 to 0.6 appear at the western edge over Lake Victoria (with an SOT 0 contour), the central highlands on the equator, near 3S 37.5E and along the eastern border, and from 8 June to 6 July only an SOT 0 contour and an isolated EFI cell near 0.58 remain over the central highlands.

A wet extreme is signalled for 15 to 22 June along the Somali border and the far east between the equator and 4N, where the EFI is 0.65 to 0.85, and on the north coast near 1.5S to 3.5S (0.65 to 0.75), both enclosed by a SOT zero contour. No part of Kenya has an EFI above 0.5 in any later week through 27 July. The only other feature is a small SOT contour in central Kenya on the equator for 13 to 20 July without EFI shading.

There is no meaningful wet-extreme signal in this forecast. The only shading is a faint EFI just above 0.5 on the coast near 3S and near the Somali border at 1.5N for 5 to 12 July, and an SOT 0 contour without EFI shading sits over the central highlands on the equator from 12 July to 9 August.

A weak wet-extreme signal appears for 5 to 12 July in the northeast near the Somali border between 1N and 3.5N (EFI 0.55 to 0.65) and in the far south and across the Tanzanian border near 3S to 5S (EFI 0.6 to 0.7), without SOT contours over Kenya. From 12 July to 2 August only isolated weak cells remain in the southwest and on the coast near 3S. For 26 July to 16 August an SOT 0 contour sits over the central highlands on the equator near 37.5E, with an EFI of about 0.55 only in the last week.

There is essentially no wet-extreme signal in this forecast. The only shading is a single cell of EFI about 0.6 with an SOT 0 contour over the central highlands on the equator near 37.5E for 28 July to 4 August, and all panels from 4 August to 8 September are blank.

Only a weak wet-extreme signal is present for 15 to 22 August, with EFI values of 0.55 to 0.65 in the northeast along the Somali and Ethiopian borders between 0.5N and 4.5N and in one cell near the southern border around 3S, and almost no supporting SOT contour. For 22 to 29 August isolated cells of 0.55 to 0.65 remain on the coast near 3S and south of the border near 4.5S. No EFI shading above 0.5 appears from 5 September onward, although a SOT zero contour covers the coast and the east for 19 to 26 September.

A weak to moderate wet-extreme signal is present for 28 August to 4 September along the eastern border from 3S to 4.5N (EFI 0.55 to 0.7) and in the far south near 4.5S 36E, where the EFI reaches about 0.8 with an SOT 0 contour. There is no signal from 4 to 18 September. Only isolated weak cells remain afterward, on the coast near 3S for 18 to 25 September and over the central highlands on the equator for 2 to 9 October, each with EFI below 0.6.

There is no wet-extreme signal for 5 to 12 September. For 12 to 19 September a weak signal (EFI 0.55 to 0.7) appears along the eastern border from the equator to 3N, partly enclosed by an SOT 0 contour, with isolated weak cells on the south coast and in the central highlands. The weeks of 19 September to 3 October show no signal, and from 3 to 17 October only small cells of EFI 0.55 to 0.6 appear over the central highlands on the equator and in the west near 1.5N.

A wet-extreme signal for 20 to 27 September covers the east and the coast, with EFI 0.7 to 0.85 between the equator and 3S near 40E to 41E and 0.6 to 0.75 up to 3N, all enclosed by SOT contours of 0 and 1. For 27 September to 4 October only a weak signal remains on the eastern border near the equator (EFI 0.55 to 0.65). From 4 to 25 October small areas of EFI 0.55 to 0.7 appear over the central highlands on the equator, the south coast and the west near 1.5N, with SOT 0 contours around them, and by 25 October to 1 November only a weak cell remains in the centre.

A wet-extreme signal for 1 to 8 October covers the centre, east and south east of 36E, with EFI 0.6 to 0.75 and the highest values of about 0.75 in the central highlands near 1.5S and on the coast near 2.5S, where an SOT 0 contour encloses the core near 37.5E. For 8 to 22 October the signal weakens to EFI 0.55 to 0.7 in small areas on the coast and the eastern border south of the equator, the central highlands near 37.5E and the west near 1.5N, each partly enclosed by SOT contours. From 22 October onward the EFI is mostly below 0.55 and only scattered SOT contours remain, with nothing from 5 November.

A wet-extreme signal covers most of central, eastern and southern Kenya for 5 to 12 October, with EFI 0.6 to 0.8 and highest values of about 0.8 in the central highlands south of the equator, where an SOT 0 contour encloses the core, and a second SOT contour on the coast near 2S to 3S. For 12 to 19 October the signal shrinks to the coast and the eastern border south of the equator (EFI 0.6 to 0.75) and to the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N (EFI about 0.75 inside the SOT 0 contour), with weaker values near 3N in the northeast. From 19 October onward there is no EFI signal, only small isolated SOT contours.

A wet extreme is signalled for 11 to 18 October in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N, where the EFI reaches 0.8 to 0.9 and is enclosed by SOT contours of 0 and 1, and along the eastern border with Somalia and the northeast, where the EFI is 0.6 to 0.8 with positive SOT. For 18 to 25 October a weaker signal (EFI 0.55 to 0.7, SOT above 0) sits over central Kenya between the equator and 3S near 37.5E. Only isolated cells just above 0.5 remain for 25 October to 1 November in the south, and there is no wet-extreme signal from 1 November onward.

A strong El Nino is in place and forecast to persist, with the relative Nino3.4 index having risen from +0.8 C in May to about +2.5 C in August and September. The ACCESS-S2 run of 10 October takes the ensemble mean to about +3.4 C in October and a peak near +3.7 C in November and December, before a decline to about +3.0 C in February and +2.4 C in March 2027. Every member stays far above the +0.8 C El Nino threshold through March and the spread is small, roughly half a degree around the mean.

The relative Nino3.4 index stood at +2.76 C in the week to 11 October 2026, far above the +0.8 C El Nino threshold and still rising. The index climbed steeply from about -0.8 C in early 2026, crossed the El Nino threshold around June, and now clearly exceeds the previous peak of about +1.6 C reached in late 2023.

GEFS weeks in this plot start on 30 July rather than 28 July. For 30 July to 6 August rain is concentrated in the west between the equator and 1.5N, reaching 35 to 50 mm from the Uganda border toward 37E, with more than 50 mm near 4N on the far western edge. For 6 to 13 August 30 to 45 mm persists near the Uganda border around 1N and the coast gets about 10 mm, and from 13 August to 3 September Kenya is essentially dry, with the last two weeks showing no rain anywhere in the domain.

GEFS puts a localized maximum of 30 to 45 mm over the western highlands between 1.5N and 1S for 15 to 22 August, with about 10 mm on the south coast and virtually no rain elsewhere. From 22 August to 12 September the western maximum weakens to 15 to 30 mm along the Uganda border and the coast receives 10 to 18 mm per week. For 12 to 19 September the west drops to 8 to 15 mm while the south coast near 4.5S increases to 15 to 25 mm.

GEFS keeps Kenya nearly dry from 28 August to 2 October, with weekly totals below 5 mm over most of the country. The only consistent rain is along the coast south of 2S, at 15 to 25 mm per week and peaking near the Tanzanian border around 4.5S, plus 8 to 12 mm over the west and the central highlands between 4 and 25 September. Heavier totals above 30 mm appear only in southern Ethiopia north of 5N in the week of 25 September to 2 October.

GEFS keeps Kenya dry from 5 September to 3 October, with weekly totals below 10 mm almost everywhere and only 15 to 20 mm in the west near the Uganda border and over the central highlands for 12 to 19 September and on the south coast for 26 September to 3 October. For 3 to 10 October 35 to 45 mm falls on the south coast between 3S and 4.5S and 15 to 20 mm over the central highlands south of the equator. Heavier rain of 60 to 65 mm is confined to southern Ethiopia north of 5N in that last week.

GEFS keeps Kenya almost completely dry (below 10 mm per week) from 20 September to 11 October, apart from 20 to 35 mm along the coast north of 3S in the first week. For 11 to 18 October 30 to 45 mm falls on the south coast and 25 to 35 mm in the west near the Uganda border, while 60 to 80 mm develops north of 5N in southern Ethiopia. For 18 to 25 October the south coast near 4S reaches 60 to 75 mm and the northeast toward the Ethiopian border 70 to 80 mm, with 25 to 35 mm over the west and the central highlands and a dry north-centre.

GEFS keeps Kenya almost entirely below 10 mm for 1 to 8 October, with 60 to 70 mm only in southern Ethiopia north of 5N. For 8 to 22 October rain is confined to the south coast between 2S and 4.5S (50 to 65 mm) and the northeast toward the Ethiopian and Somali borders (40 to 55 mm), with the interior dry. From 22 October to 5 November a band of 35 to 50 mm develops from the west across the central highlands just south of the equator, peaking near 60 mm around 37.5E, while the northwest and the eastern interior stay below 15 mm.

GEFS keeps nearly all of Kenya below 10 mm for 5 to 12 October, with heavy rain of 90 to 110 mm confined to southern Ethiopia north of 5N. For 12 to 19 October 50 to 65 mm falls along the coast south of 1.5S and in the west near the Uganda border around 1N, while the interior stays dry. From 19 October to 9 November a band of 30 to 50 mm develops from the west across the central highlands along the equator, locally near 60 mm close to Lake Victoria, while the north-centre and the east remain below 15 mm.

GEFS keeps most of Kenya nearly dry for 11 to 18 October, with rainfall confined to the west near the Uganda border around 1N (locally 60 to 100 mm) and a band above 100 mm north of 5N in southern Ethiopia. The wettest week is 25 October to 1 November, with 60 to 90 mm across western and central Kenya along the equator and 70 to 90 mm in the northeast toward the Ethiopian border. From 1 to 15 November 30 to 60 mm persist over the southwest and central highlands, and the northwest stays below 15 mm throughout.

OLR anomalies averaged over 15S to 15N show persistent enhanced convection over the central and eastern Pacific between about 180 and 110W since late July, with suppressed convection over the Indian Ocean and Maritime Continent between 60E and 150E, a low-frequency pattern consistent with El Nino. Over Africa and the western Indian Ocean (0 to 60E) anomalies have been weak, with brief Kelvin wave activity around 25 September to 2 October. The CFS forecast from 9 October keeps suppression over the eastern Indian Ocean near 80E to 110E through late October, with only weakly enhanced convection near 60E in mid October and continued enhancement over the central Pacific.

A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is established and forecast to peak in the coming weeks, with the index up from -0.2 C in May to about +0.65 C in September. The ACCESS-S2 run of 10 October puts the ensemble mean at +1.0 C in October and about +1.1 C in November, easing to +0.85 C in December and dropping below the +0.4 C positive threshold in January 2027, then near +0.1 C in February and March. Member spread in November is wide, from about +0.6 to +1.7 C, but nearly all members stay positive through December.

The IOD index was +0.88 C in the week to 11 October 2026, above the +0.4 C positive threshold and at its highest value of the year. The index has risen from about -0.4 C in mid 2026 after a short positive spell earlier in the year, and follows a strongly negative event that bottomed out near -2.0 C in November 2025.

The Intertropical Front in the third dekad of September 2026 sat well north of its normal position over West Africa, near 21N at 15W and 19N between 10W and the Greenwich meridian against a normal of about 17.5N, and close to normal east of 10E at 14 to 15N. Compared with the previous dekad the front retreated south by 1 to 2 degrees between 5E and 30E while holding its position in the west. Dekadal rainfall of 100 to 200 mm fell along the Guinea coast and over Nigeria and Cameroon, with 50 to 100 mm across the Sahel belt, 25 to 75 mm over the Ethiopian highlands and mostly less than 10 mm over Kenya outside the west.

ECMWF S2S was too wet over most of Kenya for the week of 28 September to 4 October, with forecast minus CHIRPS biases of +5 to +18 mm across the centre and east. The wet bias was largest at week 1 (init 28 September) and week 2 (init 21 September), reaching +15 to +18 mm in the northeast between 2N and 4N and in the south-centre and on the south coast. The only dry bias, -15 to -20 mm, sat in the western cell near 1.5N where CHIRPS observed 20 to 30 mm, and the week-3 forecast (init 14 September) had the smallest errors overall.

For the week of 28 September to 4 October, CHIRPS observed less than 10 mm over most of Kenya, with 20 to 30 mm only in the west near 1.5N, while ECMWF S2S forecast more widespread totals of 10 to 30 mm at all four lead weeks. Against the 5 mm threshold the forecasts scored hits in the west along the equator, in the east along the Somali border and on the south coast at every lead. Central and southern Kenya were false alarms at week 1 (init 28 September), week 2 and week 4, and the week-3 forecast (init 14 September) verified best, so the shorter leads gave no extra confidence for this week.

Daily CHIRPS rainfall averaged over the Kenya OND region stayed below 1 mm per day and close to climatology through August and the first half of September. A spike of about 5 mm per day occurred around 21 September, followed by days of 2.4 to 2.9 mm in late September and about 2.6 mm in early October, all above the climatological 1 to 1.5 mm per day for that time. Climatology rises to 4 to 5 mm per day in November, so the main season is still ahead.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall for the week starting 29 September was light over most of the Kenya OND region, at 1 to 10 mm. The exception was the far east on the Somali border between about 2N and 3N, where 40 to 100 mm fell, with 20 to 50 mm in the far north across the Ethiopian border and isolated totals of 20 to 40 mm on the eastern slopes of the central highlands. The coast received 5 to 15 mm.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall over the Kenya OND region stayed close to climatology at 2 to 3.5 mm per week from early August to mid September. The last two observed weeks, in late September and early October, each brought about 8 mm, against a climatology of roughly 4 and 6 mm. The season is therefore starting slightly ahead of normal, but the climatological ramp to 15 mm per week by mid October and a peak near 30 mm in early November is still to come.

Weekly rainfall over the Kenya OND region was within half a standard deviation of normal from early August to mid September, with z-scores between -0.5 and +0.45. The week around 20 September stood out at about +2.1, and the most recent observed week was modestly above normal at about +0.3.

Week-1 rainfall errors against CHIRPS over Kenya grew through the four verifying weeks from 7 September to 4 October as the rains started. ECMWF ENS had the largest MAE in every week, rising from 5.0 to 15.8 mm per week, and KMSA downscaled went from the lowest error (1.7 mm) in the first week to 13.1 mm in the last. AIFS and GEFS were the most stable at 3 to 6 mm and had the lowest errors in the week of 28 September to 4 October (about 5 mm), while ECMWF ER reached 9.1 mm; Cumulus AI is only available for the first two weeks, at about 3 mm.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall over Kenya stayed at 2 to 9 mm per week from early August to early October 2026, close to the analog years 2006, 2015 and 2023 and well below 2019, which had already climbed to 40 to 58 mm by early October. The downscaled S2S ensemble mean from the 11 October run gives about 23 mm per week for the two weeks from mid October, rising to 28 mm and then about 38 mm in the week starting in early November. The one-sigma range widens from roughly 14 to 34 mm at the start to 14 to 63 mm by early November, with individual members between about 5 and more than 90 mm, and the mean tracks the 2006 and 2015 analogs rather than the 2023 peak near 97 mm.

The MJO has recently weakened into the unit circle after several weeks in phases 8 and 1 (Western Hemisphere and Africa) at an amplitude of 1 to 1.5. The bias-corrected ECMWF ensemble mean for 12 to 26 October starts in phase 2 just outside the circle, drifts into the circle around 16 to 20 October, and re-emerges weakly in phases 2 to 3 (Indian Ocean) by 26 October at an amplitude of about 1.3. Most members stay in the Indian Ocean half of the diagram at amplitudes of 1 to 2, so the signal is weak to marginal with modest eastward propagation.

The bias-corrected GEFS ensemble mean for 12 to 26 October keeps the MJO just outside the unit circle, starting in phase 1 (Western Hemisphere and Africa) at an amplitude near 1.2 and moving slowly into phase 2 (Indian Ocean) with an amplitude of about 1.4 by 26 October. Propagation is slow and the member spread is large, with a few members reaching amplitudes of 2 to 3 in phases 2 and 3 and others collapsing into the circle. The observed track of the past weeks sat in phases 8 and 1 before weakening.

Observed 7-day OLR anomalies show enhanced convection over the Sahel and northern Africa between 10N and 25N from 21 September to 4 October, shifting to West Africa and the eastern Atlantic in the week of 5 to 11 October, with suppressed convection over the Arabian Sea east of 60E throughout. The CFS forecast for 12 to 18 October places strongly enhanced convection (-42 to -54 W m-2) over the western equatorial Indian Ocean near 5N between 60E and 80E, associated with MJO and equatorial Rossby wave contours. That centre moves south of the equator near 60E for 19 to 25 October with strong suppression east of 80E, and anomalies over Africa are weak from 26 October to 8 November.

Station rainfall over the past month was heaviest in the second half of September, with daily peaks of about 32 mm at Eldoret on 17 September, 33 mm at Mombasa on 19 September, 28 to 30 mm at Kisumu on 19 and 24 September and 37 mm at Nakuru on 23 September. Early October was quieter, with daily totals below 10 mm at all five stations, before renewed falls of about 17 mm at Mombasa on 10 October and 28 mm at Eldoret on 11 October. Nairobi stayed nearly dry throughout, never exceeding about 5 mm in a day.

Daily mean temperatures over the past month were steady at Mombasa (25 to 27 C) and clearly lower inland, with Kisumu at 19 to 22 C and a peak near 24 C on 4 October, and Nakuru and Eldoret at 15 to 19 C. Nairobi warmed gradually from 16 to 18 C in mid September to about 20 C in early October. All five stations show a sharp drop on the last day plotted, 13 October, which should be treated with caution.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 15 to 22 June puts 30 to 55 mm along the coast, heaviest on the south coast and just offshore south of 4S, and 25 to 35 mm across the Somali border east of 41E, with the interior below 5 mm. For 22 to 29 June the coast eases to 10 to 18 mm and the rain shifts to the west, with 20 to 35 mm and isolated cells near 60 mm along the Uganda border and the western highlands between 2N and 1S. Totals of 40 to 60 mm lie north of 6N in southern Ethiopia in the second week.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 28 June to 5 July puts 20 to 35 mm along the western edge of the domain north of 2N and above 50 mm over the Ethiopian highlands near 6N, with scattered cells in the west near the equator and below 3 mm over the rest of Kenya. For 5 to 12 July the western rain broadens to 35 to 50 mm from 1S to 5N along the Uganda border, with cells above 50 mm near Lake Victoria. The coast picks up 15 to 20 mm and the far south coast near the Tanzanian border 30 to 45 mm in the second week.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 5 to 12 July puts 30 to 45 mm on the south coast between 4S and 5.5S and over the Ethiopian highlands near 6N, with isolated cells of about 40 mm in the central highlands near 1S. For 12 to 19 July the heaviest rain, 35 to 45 mm, is along the western edge of the domain from Lake Victoria north to 6N, while the coast drops to 10 to 15 mm. The north-centre and east of Kenya stay below 3 mm in both weeks.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 28 July to 4 August puts 25 to 38 mm across the west from Lake Victoria north along the Uganda border to 5N, with below 3 mm over the centre, north and east. For 4 to 11 August the west still gets 20 to 35 mm between the equator and 3N, and 15 to 25 mm develops along the coast south of 1.5S. The interior east of 37E stays nearly dry in both weeks.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 15 to 22 August has scattered totals of 20 to 35 mm over the west and southwest between 1.5N and 1S, 12 to 20 mm over the southeast coast, and less than 5 mm across the north and centre. For 22 to 29 August the western maximum strengthens to 25 to 35 mm along the Uganda border from 3N to the equator, with isolated cells above 30 mm near the southern border around 3S and on the south coast. The north-central and eastern interior stay dry in both weeks.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 28 August to 4 September puts 20 to 29 mm along the coast between 1.5S and 4.5S and in scattered cells over the southwest and central highlands, with below 3 mm across the northwest and north. For 4 to 11 September the rain shifts west, with 20 to 29 mm near the Uganda border between the equator and 1.5N and 20 to 25 mm on the south coast. The north and centre stay nearly dry in both weeks.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 5 to 12 September is nearly dry, with below 5 mm over most of Kenya and 10 to 20 mm only in the west and along the eastern border. For 12 to 19 September rainfall increases in the west, reaching above 40 mm over Lake Victoria and near the Uganda border at 1.5N, with 30 to 45 mm on the south coast and in southern Ethiopia. The northwest and the centre stay below 5 mm in both weeks.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 20 to 27 September puts 40 to 55 mm along the coast between 1.5S and 3.5S and above 50 mm north of 4.5N in southern Ethiopia, with 25 to 40 mm in the west near Lake Victoria and below 5 mm across the northwest and the north-centre. For 27 September to 4 October the heaviest totals shift west, with above 50 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria just south of the equator and 40 to 55 mm over the central highlands near 37.5E. The north-centre stays below 10 mm in both weeks, and the coast drops to 25 to 40 mm in the second week.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 1 to 8 October puts 60 to 90 mm in isolated cells over the central highlands just south of the equator near 37.5E and on the south coast near 4.5S, with 30 to 45 mm over the east and below 10 mm across the northwest and the southwest. For 8 to 15 October rainfall increases widely, reaching 80 to 95 mm on the south coast between 2S and 4.5S, at the western edge over Lake Victoria on the equator and over the central highlands near 37E. The east and northeast get 40 to 60 mm in the second week, while the northwest and the far southwest stay at 10 to 20 mm.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 5 to 12 October puts 60 to 90 mm over the northeast north of 3N near the Somali border, above 100 mm in the central highlands just south of the equator, and 50 to 70 mm along the south coast, while the northwest and the area along the southern border stay below 15 mm. For 12 to 19 October the rain intensifies and broadens, with 80 to 100 mm across the east from the northeast to the coast, above 100 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria and in the central highlands, and 40 to 60 mm in the west. Only the far south interior near the Tanzanian border stays below 15 mm in the second week.

The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 11 to 18 October puts 60 to 90 mm along the eastern border and north coast, across the northeast and north of 4N, and along the western border, with the interior from the northwest down to the southern border mostly below 15 mm. For 18 to 25 October the rain shifts south, with 60 to 90 mm in a band from Lake Victoria across the central highlands between the equator and 2S and 30 to 50 mm over the east and the coast. The northwest is the driest area in both weeks at 10 to 20 mm or less.

Kenya is virtually dry in the ECMWF S2S ensemble mean from 15 to 29 January (below 2 mm), with only 10 to 20 mm at the far southwestern edge of the domain over Lake Victoria and northern Tanzania. Rain builds in the southwest from 29 January, reaching 30 to 50 mm at the western edge and 15 to 20 mm in southwest Kenya in the week of 5 to 12 February. From 12 to 26 February the southwest near the Tanzanian border receives 20 to 35 mm and the central highlands 10 to 15 mm, while the north and east stay below 5 mm throughout.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 10 to 17 February is below 5 mm across almost all of Kenya, with rain confined to the southwest near Lake Victoria (about 70 mm at the western edge near 1.5S) and 25 to 35 mm in northern Tanzania. For 17 February to 3 March the wet area expands over the southwest and central highlands, with 30 to 40 mm near 37.5E on the equator, more than 100 mm at the western edge near 1.5S in the first week and 60 to 80 mm south of the border. From 3 to 24 March the southwest keeps 25 to 60 mm per week, while the north and east stay below 10 mm throughout.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 5 to 12 March is high over the southwest and south, with 80 to 90 mm at the western edge near 1.5S and over northern Tanzania, 60 to 75 mm in the southwest and central highlands just south of the equator and 30 to 45 mm across the west and north, while the east stays below 15 mm. The week of 12 to 19 March is much drier, below 10 mm over most of the north and east, with 40 to 60 mm only at the western edge and near the southern border. From 19 March to 16 April the southwest and central highlands get 30 to 45 mm per week, about 70 to 80 mm at the western edge near 1.5S, and the north 15 to 30 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 20 to 27 March is widespread at 40 to 60 mm, with 70 to 80 mm in the west near 2N and in the southwest near 3S, more than 100 mm over Lake Victoria and 80 to 100 mm on the south coast, while the northeast along the Somali border stays below 25 mm. Totals drop sharply from 27 March, to 20 to 40 mm over most areas and less than 15 mm in the north-centre between 2N and 4N. From 3 April to 1 May the southwest and south-centre hold 30 to 50 mm per week and the north and east 15 to 30 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 10 to 24 April is modest over Kenya, mostly 5 to 30 mm per week, with 50 to 60 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria and about 40 mm in the central highlands near 1.5S in the first week, and the largest totals (70 to more than 100 mm) offshore and on the Tanzanian coast near 5S. The week of 24 April to 1 May is the wettest, with about 95 mm at the western edge near 1.5S, 60 to 80 mm along the Uganda border and 25 to 40 mm across much of the north, centre and east. From 1 to 22 May the west keeps 50 to 65 mm at the edge of the domain and the south coast 40 to 65 mm, while the interior falls back below 15 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 20 to 27 April is 30 to 45 mm across the north and west, 60 to 75 mm at the western edge of the domain over Lake Victoria, and 60 to 90 mm on the south coast and offshore south of 3S. The week of 27 April to 4 May is the wettest, with 55 to 70 mm over the western half between 2N and 2S and the central highlands, 90 to 115 mm over Lake Victoria and 40 to 60 mm on the coast. Totals then decline countrywide, with the north and east below 15 mm by 18 May and only 20 to 30 mm left in the west and on the coast by 25 May to 1 June.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 5 to 12 May is heaviest in the west, reaching 55 to 68 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria and 45 to 50 mm near the Uganda border at 2N and at 36E on the equator, with about 40 mm over the central highlands and 20 to 25 mm on the coast. For 12 to 19 May the west keeps 40 to 55 mm, peaking near 2N 34.5E, and the coast near 3S to 4.5S gets 35 to 45 mm, while the north-centre stays below 10 mm. From 19 May to 16 June the interior dries to below 5 mm, the west drops to 10 to 30 mm per week and the coast near 3S to 4S stays at 20 to 40 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 25 May to 1 June is concentrated on the coast, peaking at about 65 mm near 3S, with 15 to 20 mm in the west near the Uganda border and below 10 mm across the interior. For 1 to 8 June the maximum shifts west, with 40 to 45 mm near the Uganda border at 2N and over Lake Victoria on the equator, while the coast near 4.5S keeps 35 to 40 mm. From 8 June to 6 July the interior stays below 5 mm, the west gets 15 to 22 mm per week and the coast near 3S 25 to 40 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 15 to 22 June is concentrated on the coast and across the Somali border, with 35 to 45 mm near the north coast around 3S and 12 to 18 mm along the eastern border, while most of the interior stays below 5 mm. From 22 June to 27 July the coast eases to 15 to 30 mm per week and the west along the Uganda border receives 15 to 25 mm, peaking near 2N. The northern and central interior remain almost dry (below 3 mm) in every week.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 28 June to 5 July is limited to the west, with about 20 mm near the Uganda border at 2N and 25 mm further west, while the centre, north and east stay below 3 mm. The week of 5 to 12 July is the wettest, with about 30 mm in the west near 2N to 3N and on the coast near 3S, and 25 mm on the south coast near 4.5S. From 12 July to 9 August the west keeps 20 to 33 mm per week, peaking near 2N 34.5E in the week of 2 to 9 August, and the coast near 3S gets 15 to 25 mm, while the interior from the north to the southern border remains below 3 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 5 to 12 July is highest on the south coast and across the Tanzanian border near 5S (20 to 30 mm), with 10 to 15 mm in the west and below 3 mm over the north, centre and east. From 12 July to 2 August the rain shifts to the west near the Uganda border, reaching 25 to 35 mm around 2N, while the coast near 3S keeps 15 to 25 mm. For 2 to 16 August the western maximum strengthens to about 38 mm near 2N 34.5E, with 25 to 30 mm along the western edge of the domain, and the north-centre and east stay below 3 mm throughout.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 28 July to 4 August is confined to the west, with 30 to 35 mm at the western edge near 1.5N and about 25 mm over Lake Victoria, while the centre, north and east stay below 3 mm. The week of 4 to 11 August peaks at about 44 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N, with about 25 mm on the coast near 3S. From 11 August to 8 September the west gets 15 to 30 mm per week and the south coast 10 to 20 mm, while the rest of Kenya stays below 5 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 15 to 22 August is confined to the west along the Uganda border and the Lake Victoria basin (15 to 25 mm) and to the south coast (12 to 20 mm), with the north and centre of Kenya below 5 mm. The same west and coast pattern holds through 12 September with little change in amounts. From 12 to 26 September totals rise to 25 to 35 mm at the western edge of the domain and to 20 to 25 mm on the coast, and 35 to 45 mm appear north of 5N in southern Ethiopia.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 28 August to 4 September is below 5 mm over nearly all of Kenya, with about 28 mm on the coast near 3S. Through September the west near the Uganda border and Lake Victoria picks up 15 to 30 mm per week and the coast 15 to 25 mm, while the north and centre stay below 5 mm. The week of 2 to 9 October is the wettest, with 40 to 50 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria and near 1.5N, 30 to 35 mm on the coast near 3S and 30 to 50 mm in the far northeast toward the Ethiopian border.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 5 to 12 September is below 5 mm over nearly all of Kenya, with 15 to 20 mm only on the south coast and near the Ethiopian border. From 12 September to 3 October weekly totals stay below 10 mm in the north and centre, with 25 to 40 mm in the west near the Uganda border and over Lake Victoria and 20 to 25 mm on the south coast. Rain increases from 3 October, and the week of 10 to 17 October is the wettest at 60 to 65 mm in the west near 1.5N and over Lake Victoria, 45 to 50 mm on the coast near 3S and 35 to 40 mm in the northeast and the central highlands.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 20 to 27 September is below 10 mm across most of the interior, with about 60 mm on the coast near 3S and 25 to 35 mm along the eastern border and the north coast. The week of 27 September to 4 October is drier still, with the northwest and centre below 5 mm and 20 to 30 mm only in the east. Rain builds from 4 October in the west, reaching 65 to 80 mm near the Uganda border at 1.5N and over Lake Victoria in the weeks of 4 to 18 October, with 50 to 65 mm on the south coast, and from 18 October to 1 November it peaks near 90 mm over Lake Victoria at 1.5S, with 60 to 65 mm in the central highlands on the equator.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 1 to 8 October is modest, with 40 to 50 mm on the coast near 3S, 20 to 35 mm over the east and northeast, and below 10 mm across the northwest, north-centre and far southwest. The weeks of 8 to 22 October are wetter, with 70 to 85 mm at the western edge over Lake Victoria and in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N, 65 to 80 mm on the south coast and 45 to 55 mm over the northeast and the central highlands. From 22 October to 12 November the heaviest rain sits in the southwest and over Lake Victoria, peaking near 90 mm at 1.5S in the week of 29 October to 5 November, while the north-centre stays at 10 to 25 mm.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 5 to 12 October is highest at the western edge of the domain over Lake Victoria and on the coast near 3S (about 60 to 65 mm), with 40 to 55 mm over the northeast, while the north-centre and the far southwest stay below 10 mm. The week of 12 to 19 October is the wettest, with about 95 mm in the west near the Uganda border at 1.5N, about 80 mm over Lake Victoria and 75 to 80 mm on the south coast. From 19 October to 16 November most of Kenya gets 20 to 40 mm per week, the north-centre stays below 15 mm, and 60 to 80 mm recur over Lake Victoria.

ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 11 to 18 October is heaviest in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N (about 100 mm) and over the northeast toward the Ethiopian and Somali borders (40 to 70 mm), while central and southern Kenya stay below 10 mm. From 18 October to 8 November the rain spreads into the southwest and the central highlands with 30 to 50 mm per week, and 70 to 95 mm at the western edge of the domain over Lake Victoria. The north remains mostly below 20 mm per week through 22 November.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 10 to 24 April is patchy, with 40 to 80 mm over the central highlands near 37.5E, near the southern border around 3S and on the south coast, while the north stays mostly below 10 mm. The week of 24 April to 1 May is by far the wettest, with large areas above 80 mm over the west and Lake Victoria from 3N to 4.5S, over the central highlands just south of the equator and along the northern border. From 1 to 22 May maxima above 80 mm persist over the west near the equator, the central highlands and the coast near 2S, while the north-centre and east dry out.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 20 to 27 April exceeds 80 mm in the west between Lake Victoria and the western highlands, in the central highlands near the equator and locally on the north coast, with the north-central interior below 10 mm. The week of 27 April to 4 May is by far the wettest, with 60 to 98 mm across the west, several maxima above 90 mm in the north-centre between 2N and 4N, the central highlands, the north coast and near the southern border, and only the eastern interior below 20 mm. From 4 May the rain contracts to the west, the central highlands and a 70 to 98 mm strip along the south coast, and by 25 May to 1 June most of the country is below 20 mm.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 5 to 12 May exceeds 65 mm over the west and Lake Victoria between 1.5N and 1S, over the central highlands just south of the equator and on the south coast near the Tanzanian border, while the north-centre and east stay dry. For 12 to 19 May the western maximum expands from 2.5N to 1.5S, with large areas above 65 mm, and the coast near 2S exceeds 60 mm. From 19 May to 16 June the west eases to 30 to 50 mm per week, while the coast near 2S keeps 50 to 65 mm or more, peaking in the week of 9 to 16 June.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 25 May to 1 June exceeds 100 mm along the coast from 1S to 4.5S, with 40 to 60 mm in the west near Lake Victoria and a nearly dry interior. For 1 to 8 June the coast near 2S to 3S still exceeds 90 mm, the west between 1.5N and 0.5S gets 40 to 70 mm and a cell of about 60 mm appears in the central highlands. From 8 June to 6 July the coast near 2S stays at 80 to 100 mm per week, easing to 60 to 80 mm in the last week, while the west gets 20 to 50 mm and the north and centre stay dry.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 15 to 22 June exceeds 60 mm on the north coast and its hinterland around 1S to 2.5S, with 15 to 30 mm along the rest of the coast and only 10 to 20 mm in the west. From 22 June to 13 July the coastal strip holds 30 to 55 mm, with the maximum moving to the south coast in the week of 29 June to 6 July, and the western highlands near the equator pick up 30 to 50 mm. From 13 to 27 July the main maximum is in the west (40 to 55 mm around 35E), and the northern and eastern interior stay dry throughout.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 28 June to 5 July is above 60 mm on the coast near 2S and 30 to 50 mm in the west near Lake Victoria, with the rest of Kenya below 10 mm. From 5 July to 9 August the west between 1.5N and 1.5S is the wettest part of Kenya, with 40 to 60 mm per week, exceeding 60 mm near 0.5S 35.5E for 19 to 26 July and across 0 to 1N near 35E for 2 to 9 August. The centre, north and east stay essentially dry, while totals above 60 mm recur every week north of 6N in southern Ethiopia.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 5 to 12 July is concentrated on the coast near 2S (above 50 mm) and the south coast near 4S (40 to 50 mm), with only small cells of 30 to 40 mm in the west. From 12 July onward the west near Lake Victoria and the Uganda border becomes the wettest part of Kenya, rising from 40 to 60 mm per week to more than 60 mm between the equator and 1N near 35E in the weeks of 26 July to 16 August. The centre, north and east remain essentially dry, while totals above 60 mm persist north of 6N in southern Ethiopia.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 28 July to 4 August exceeds 60 mm in the west near Lake Victoria and the Uganda border between the equator and 1.5N, with the centre, north and east essentially dry. From 4 August to 8 September the west keeps 30 to 55 mm per week, largest just north of the equator near 35E, while the coast gets 10 to 25 mm. Heavy totals above 60 mm also appear north of 6N in southern Ethiopia every week, and the rest of Kenya stays below 5 mm.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 15 to 22 August is 25 to 40 mm in the west between the Uganda border and about 36E, and 15 to 30 mm in a narrow strip along the coast, with the rest of the country dry. The western maximum stays above 40 mm near the equator through 12 September and the coastal strip holds 20 to 35 mm. From 12 to 26 September the west intensifies into a broad area above 40 mm from Lake Victoria to 35.5E, and in the week of 19 to 26 September more than 40 mm is also indicated on the north coast and its hinterland.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 28 August to 4 September is below 5 mm over most of Kenya, with 35 to 45 mm only in the east near the Somali border just south of the equator. From 4 to 25 September the west around Lake Victoria and the Uganda border gets 30 to 50 mm per week, and from 18 September the coast north and south of 2S exceeds 50 mm. For 25 September to 9 October the heaviest totals, above 50 mm, are along the eastern border south of the equator, in the west, in the northeast near 3.5N and on the south coast, while the northwest stays dry.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 5 to 12 September is confined to the west near Lake Victoria and the Uganda border (locally 30 to 50 mm), with the rest of Kenya below 5 mm. From 12 September to 3 October the west keeps 40 to 65 mm per week, and the north coast near 1.5S picks up more than 65 mm from 19 September. From 3 to 17 October heavy rain becomes widespread, above 65 mm over the east between the equator and 3N, along the coast, over the central highlands and in the west, while the northwest stays dry throughout.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 20 September to 4 October stays below 15 mm over most of the north and centre, with 30 to 50 mm in the west near Lake Victoria and locally above 80 mm on the north coast near 1.5S. From 4 October rain spreads quickly, with maxima above 90 mm in the northeast near 3.5N, over the central highlands just south of the equator, in the west and on the south coast. The weeks of 11 October to 1 November are the wettest, with large areas above 90 mm over the west, the central highlands on the equator, the northeast and the coast, while the northwest stays below 15 mm throughout.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 1 to 8 October is concentrated in the southeast and on the south coast between 2.5S and 4.5S, locally above 90 mm, while the north and west stay mostly below 15 mm. From 8 to 29 October maxima above 90 mm persist over the central highlands just south of the equator near 37.5E and on the coast, joined by the west near Lake Victoria and the northeast between 1.5N and 3.5N near the Somali border. The weeks of 29 October to 12 November are the wettest, with large areas above 90 mm over the central highlands, the west and the east near 2N, while the northwest remains below 15 mm.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 5 to 12 October exceeds 120 mm in the northeast between 2N and 4N near the Somali border, over the central highlands just south of the equator near 37.5E and in the southeast near 1.5S, while the northwest and the south interior stay below 15 mm. The week of 12 to 19 October brings more than 100 mm along the whole eastern border and the coast, around Lake Victoria and over the central highlands. Totals ease from 19 October to 2 November with maxima above 100 mm only over the central highlands, then a large area above 120 mm develops over the central highlands between the equator and 3S in the weeks of 2 to 16 November, while the northwest stays dry throughout.

Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 11 to 18 October exceeds 100 mm in the west near the Uganda border, along the eastern border and the north coast, and in the far north across the Ethiopian border, while the central interior and the south stay below 10 mm. From 18 October onward the maximum shifts to the central highlands just east of 37E near the equator, where weekly totals exceed 120 mm in the weeks of 18 to 25 October and 1 to 8 November. The week of 1 to 8 November is the wettest overall, with additional maxima of 90 to 120 mm in the southwest and near the southern border around 3S, and the northwest remains dry in every week.
